items.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003
items.q: Even though he reflected and he was wide open to the music of Ravel, Debussy, Satie, you name it, all the great European art music composers

ctx.x: Contemporary music, yeah. Which is cool.

But jazz, recognizing its roots in Africa and coming through the African-American experiences and then incorporating all the other elements that it has done, you know I think that it’s important that that be emphasized in all jazz degree curriculums. And also it should be taught on the elementary, secondary and the higher education levels. Because Mary Lou Williams came up with this thing about the living tree of jazz. And if we are going to recognize this art form as a living tree you have to recognize the…
Would it be safe to say that the melodic part of the African music that filtered into jazz was more of a vocal nature, the way they sang?
